test_title: SSC CHSL 2025 Tier-1 (Held On: 25 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Who among the following criticised the Moderates for their "politics of prayer"?

I. Bepin Chandra Pal

II. Bal Gangadhar Tilak

III. Lala Lajpat Rai
solution:
The correct answer is __**I, II, and III**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Bepin Chandra Pal**, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, and **Lala Lajpat Rai** were prominent leaders of the Extremist faction in the Indian National Movement. They criticized the Moderates for their approach of petitioning and praying to the British government for reforms instead of taking assertive actions. ***Hence, all three leaders are correct.*** 
• The Moderates followed a strategy of peaceful and constitutional methods like petitions, resolutions, speeches, and delegations to achieve their objectives. This was referred to as the "politics of prayer" by their critics. 
• **Bepin Chandra Pal:** He was a key figure in the Extremist movement and believed in direct action rather than relying on constitutional methods. Pal criticized the Moderates for their lack of urgency and assertiveness. ***Statement I is correct.*** 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:** He advocated for Swaraj (self-rule) and was a proponent of aggressive nationalism. He was one of the most vocal critics of the Moderates and called for mass mobilization and active resistance against colonial rule. ***Statement II is correct.*** 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:** Known as the "Lion of Punjab," Rai supported the idea of direct action and criticized the Moderates for their reliance on petitions and negotiations with the British. ***Statement III is correct.*** 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Moderates:** 
• The Moderates were a faction within the Indian National Congress during its early years (1885–1905). 
• They believed in constitutional methods to achieve political reforms and sought cooperation with the British government. 
• Prominent leaders included **Dadabhai Naoroji**, **Gopal Krishna Gokhale**, and **Pherozeshah Mehta**. 
• Their methods included drafting petitions, presenting memorandums, and holding discussions with British officials. 
• **Extremists:** 
• The Extremists emerged as a faction within the Congress after 1905, advocating for more radical methods to achieve independence. 
• They believed that the Moderates' methods were ineffective and promoted mass mobilization, boycotts, and Swadeshi (self-reliance). 
• Prominent leaders included **Bepin Chandra Pal**, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, and **Lala Lajpat Rai**. 
• They were instrumental in the Swadeshi Movement, especially after the partition of Bengal in 1905. 
• **Key Differences Between Moderates and Extremists:** 
• **Moderates:** Believed in gradual reforms through dialogue, cooperation, and constitutional methods. 
• **Extremists:** Advocated for immediate and complete independence using mass mobilization and direct action. 
• **Partition of Bengal (1905):** 
• The partition of Bengal by Lord Curzon in 1905 was a major turning point in the Indian National Movement. 
• It led to the rise of the Swadeshi Movement and increased support for the Extremists. 
• The movement focused on boycotting British goods and promoting indigenous industries. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Formation of Indian National Congress:** The Congress was established in **1885** by **A.O. Hume** with the aim of providing a platform for political dialogue and reform. 
• **Swadeshi Movement:** Initiated in **1905** as a response to the partition of Bengal, it focused on self-reliance and boycotting British products. 
• **Extremist Leaders:** Known as the "Lal-Bal-Pal" trio, **Lala Lajpat Rai**, **Bal Gangadhar Tilak**, and **Bepin Chandra Pal** played a crucial role in shaping the Indian independence movement. 
• **Delhi Durbar (1903):** Held by Lord Curzon to celebrate the coronation of King Edward VII, it showcased the British imperial authority and further alienated Indian sentiments.
